title: Real launch-site selection and range-safety criteria for the Earth spaceport, and their orbital-access consequences
question: What do real launch-site licensing and range-safety standards (e.g. FAA 14 CFR Part 420/450, EASA/ESA and national airspace and land-use rules) and orbital mechanics require of a launch site — terrain, exclusion and downrange-overflight distance, population and airspace separation, weather and transport access — and what does that imply for NOX:TER:SAUERLAND-SPACEPORT at roughly 51.3°N in the Sauerland (reachable orbital inclinations, dogleg performance penalties, achievable LEO/other orbits, feasibility of a purely suborbital or shuttle-port role), so that the current siting heuristic is either aligned to real criteria or explicitly re-scoped as a suborbital/shuttle facility?
why_now: The Earth workstream is active: docs/architecture/earth-real-geography-bootstrap.md and earth-spatial-world.md make the Sauerland the first real playable region, the Earth surface-logistics policy ends at NOX:TER:SAUERLAND-SPACEPORT and hands over to a Surface Transfer Shuttle, and lib/world/spatial/spaceportSuitability.ts plus spaceportAreaAnalysis.ts already score real terrain and OSM features with concrete thresholds (slope <= 3 deg bonus, road < 1200 m, exclusion < 250/600 m) while stating they are a planning heuristic that makes no launch-safety claim. sauerland2086Scenario.ts carries 'europeanSpaceportProgram: true' as an explicit narrative assumption. The siting logic is being coded now, so the missing real criteria are a live dependency rather than a future nice-to-have.
real_world_anchor: Launch-site licensing and range-safety standards (FAA 14 CFR Part 420/450, EASA/ESA and German airspace and planning law) together with launch-azimuth vs. target-inclination and downrange-overflight constraints from orbital mechanics.
novelty_reason: Not a rephrase of RES-20260828-BF7F1B4D: that candidate covers orbital/physical body parameters and interplanetary Hohmann travel times. This gap covers surface-to-orbit access from one specific real site — launch-site siting criteria, range-safety separation and the latitude/inclination ceiling — which is a surface-to-LEO engineering-and-standards question, not an interplanetary trajectory or body-parameter question. It is also unrelated to the LVT/space-law candidate (RES-20260828-47D98879), which is about property rights rather than launch safety.
